result.narrative:
Ford's underlying fundamentals look benign: payment behaviour shows a single open overdue notice of $450,000 (9 days past due) against a $6,000,000 credit line, and the reviewer notes there is no resolved-notification history yet to benchmark a pattern. The large body of genuine news coverage over the review window is routine stock commentary, analyst sentiment, an earnings beat, a contained supplier disruption, and a scheduled executive departure - none of it rated above minor severity and none indicating financial distress.

The Watch score of 40.9 is driven almost entirely by one item: a severity-100 "unpaid wages/employee protest" headline (LIVE01) that is explicitly tagged "[HYPOTHETICAL]" and sourced to "HYPOTHETICAL - typed in the room" rather than a real outlet, contributing 35.0 of the 40.9 total. The adjudicator challenged the verdict on this basis, finding no independent corroboration from any other source and noting that payment evidence alone (0.65 x 9.0) would sit well inside the Healthy band. The payment signal itself is thin - a first notification with no accumulation pattern yet established.

The limit system recommends reducing the TCI-EX-2026-0001 export limit from $6,000,000 to $4,862,237, sized to bring expected loss back to the 25% appetite threshold (from $1,332,720 to $1,080,000) given the current PD of 0.3085. Because that PD is itself inflated by the disputed hypothetical headline, the underwriter should treat this REDUCE recommendation with caution and decide whether to apply it in full, apply a smaller cut, or hold the limit pending verification of the wage-protest story.

A lift back toward Healthy (score below 20.0) would follow from the hypothetical news item being withdrawn, discredited, or decaying with no corroboration (it alone is currently holding the band), combined with the 9-day-past-due invoice resolving without further ageing. Conversely, real deterioration - the overdue item ageing out to 24 days past due - would push the score toward the High Risk band at 50.0, as would any genuinely sourced negative reporting corroborating distress at Ford.
